name: service
description: The service domain pack (E12, docs/decisions/011): ordinary request-driven services, the concrete test of the pipeline-core/domain-pack split E13 extracted. Landed in phases, not one epic-sized change: phase 1 (docs/decisions/016) proved the three lenses reused UNCHANGED from genai (tracing, ops, pii-governance) run against real service-domain points with zero SKILL.md edits; phase 2 (docs/decisions/017) added the anti-redundancy gate; phase 3 (docs/decisions/018) added the first S1 registry (Express, http_server_route); phase 4 (docs/decisions/019) added telemetry-cost; phase 5 (docs/decisions/020) added slo and multi-artifact lens support; phase 6 (docs/decisions/021) added dependency -- all six lenses now real; a mechanism proof (docs/decisions/022) drove S1->S9 end to end; phase 7 (docs/decisions/023) added the second S1 registry (pg, db_query); phase 8 (docs/decisions/024) added the third (node-cron, scheduled_job) and its own new imported_namespace_method_call detector shape; phase 9 (docs/decisions/028) added the fourth (amqplib, queue_producer/queue_consumer) and a genuinely new chain_hop detector shape -- amqplib's real API needs a two-hop async chained receiver resolution (connect -> createChannel -> the actual queue operation) none of the three prior shapes could express. Every registry entry is docs-grounded rather than corpus-verified (no real TS corpus repo has been run through this adapter yet -- named explicitly, same honesty precedent as the genai pack's own livekit registry). declarative_route and http_client_call are E11-TS's TypeScript adapter's own fixed passes (SP12, docs/decisions/013), previously undetected by any loaded pack (docs/decisions/014's own named gap) -- declaring them here is what makes those already-detected points visible to S3's gap model for the first time.

registries.confidence_note: Docs-grounded (Express's own public API, https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api.html), NOT corpus-verified -- no real Express repo has been run through this adapter yet, unlike every genai registry entry, which either has real corpus evidence (anthropic, 100% recall) or says so explicitly when it doesn't (livekit). Deliberately narrow: only `const app = express()` (a bare factory call assigned to a variable, the module_function_call detector shape -- oah/discovery/typescript_adapter.py's ImportResolver.resolve_factory_call, newly implemented alongside this entry, since the shape existed in schemas/domain_pack.schema.json but no adapter actually implemented it before this). Two real, deliberate exclusions from method_suffixes, not oversights: `app.all(...)`/`app.use(...)` are left out -- `use` is overwhelmingly called for plain middleware with no path argument at all (`app.use(cors())`) in real Express code, which this suffix-match alone can't distinguish from a genuine path-mounted sub-router, and including it would trade real false positives for marginal recall; `express.Router()` sub-router creation (a namespaced factory call, not a bare one) is also not covered -- a real, separate, NOT-yet-implemented receiver-creation shape. `get` is Express's own documented dual-purpose method (`app.get(name)` reads a setting; `app.get(path, ...handlers)` registers a route) -- the adapter requires 2+ call arguments before treating any of these five suffixes as a route registration, specifically to rule out the single-argument settings-getter form.

Docs-grounded (node-postgres's own docs, https://node-postgres.com/apis/client and /apis/pool), NOT corpus-verified. `Client` and `Pool` are both real, current, non-deprecated exports; both expose the same `.query(text, values?)` method (Pool.query auto-acquires/releases a pooled Client). No dual-purpose-method ambiguity the way Express's `.get()` had -- `.query()` has one meaning. Deliberately narrow to the ES-module named-import form (`import { Client, Pool } from "pg"`, real since pg v8.15 per node-postgres's own ESM docs) -- ImportResolver's existing named-import handling covers this with zero adapter code change, the same shape Anthropic/Pinecone already use. Three real, separate gaps, not silently assumed covered: CommonJS `const { Client, Pool } = require("pg")` (no registry in this pack has ever supported `require()`, a pre-existing gap, not new); the default-import-then-destructure form (`import pg from "pg"; const { Client, Pool } = pg;`, still common for pg < 8.15 and some bundler setups); and `new pg.Client()` namespace-member construction (a member-expression constructor, which `ImportResolver.resolve_constructor_call` doesn't resolve today -- the same class of gap `express.Router()` left named for Express). `postgres` (postgres.js) is a real, increasingly common alternative client with a different tagged-template API shape -- not covered, no registry entry, named here rather than guessed at.

Docs-grounded (node-cron's own README, https://github.com/node-cron/node-cron), NOT corpus-verified. `cron.schedule(cronExpression, callback)` is called directly on the default-imported module -- no constructor/factory step, the new imported_namespace_method_call shape this entry is the first consumer of (docs/decisions/024). Chosen as this pack's #1 scheduling-library registry over two real alternatives (verified via live npm download-count queries, not estimated): the `cron` package's `new CronJob(cronTime, onTick, ...)` (real, current, ~6.8M weekly downloads, but a materially different shape -- the constructor call itself IS the registration event, with no subsequent method call to suffix-match against at all; a fourth detector shape, not yet implemented, named here rather than folded in) and `node-schedule`'s `schedule.scheduleJob(...)` (same imported_namespace_method_call shape as node-cron, ~4.4M weekly downloads, not covered -- a real, additional registry entry this phase didn't also add, not because the shape is hard, just to keep this phase to one library at a time).

Docs-grounded (amqplib's own README, https://github.com/amqp-node/amqplib#connect), NOT corpus-verified. `amqp.connect(url)` is amqplib's real promise-API entry point, called directly on the default-imported module (`import amqp from "amqplib"`) -- the first hop of a real three-hop async resolution chain (connect -> createChannel -> the actual queue operation, docs/decisions/028) that none of this pack's three prior receiver-resolution shapes could express on their own. This entry contributes no surface point by itself -- it only teaches the known-name prescan that a variable assigned from (optionally awaited) `amqp.connect(...)` is a Connection, feeding the createChannel hop below. Two real, named gaps, not silently assumed covered: CommonJS `require("amqplib")` (a pre-existing gap for every registry in this pack, not new here) and amqplib's own separate callback API (`require("amqplib/callback_api")`), a structurally different, non-Promise surface this entry doesn't attempt.

Docs-grounded (amqplib's own README, https://github.com/amqp-node/amqplib#model_createChannel). `connection.createChannel()` is the second hop: a Connection resolved by the chain_hop entry above calling `.createChannel()` produces a Channel, the receiver every real queue operation (assertQueue/sendToQueue/publish/consume) is actually called on. `createConfirmChannel()` (a real, separate constructor for a confirm-mode channel) is NOT covered -- a named gap, not folded in. Like the entry above, this contributes no surface point on its own, only known-name propagation.

Docs-grounded (amqplib's own README, sendToQueue and publish sections), NOT corpus-verified. Both are real producer-side operations called on a Channel resolved through the two chain_hop entries above -- the genuinely new capability this phase adds (docs/decisions/028): a two-hop chained receiver resolution, where neither hop alone is `new X()`, a bare factory call, or a direct import binding, the three shapes every registry before this one relied on. `assertQueue` (queue/topology declaration, not itself a produce/consume event) is deliberately excluded -- a real, separate gap named here should a future phase want to detect queue-topology declaration as its own surface_kind. Note, not acted on here: `sendToQueue`/`publish` both return a plain boolean synchronously in amqplib's own API, not a Promise, unlike the two chain hops above -- irrelevant to this detector (suffix-matching doesn't care about a call's return shape) but a real fact this pack's own latency-reasoning lenses (e.g. slo) should know if they're ever pointed at these kinds.

Docs-grounded (amqplib's own README, channel.consume section), NOT corpus-verified. `channel.consume(queue, callback, options)` is amqplib's sole consumer-side pattern (no async-iterator alternative exists in core amqplib) -- called on the SAME Channel receiver as the queue_producer entry above, via the identical two-hop chain (module_to_registries resolves the two entries by which one's method_suffixes actually matches, not by sdk_module alone, since both share "amqplib#channel"). dimension: routing, matching this pack's existing queue_consumer point_kind -- an inbound entrypoint conceptually alongside http_server_route/declarative_route, not an outbound dependency.

covered_signals.caveat: Only when the framework's own router exposes a low-cardinality template to the instrumentation library -- a raw/untemplated path (e.g. AEM resolving a URL to a content path by resource type) is not covered and needs the pack's own cardinality_guard design, not this baseline.
Conditionally required ("if request has ended with an error") on the HTTP duration histograms, per docs/decisions/012 finding 6 -- not present on every data point, only error ones.
